findings.title: Denials are cached for 30s and checked before any requery, reintroducing the stale-access problem
findings.body: A denied Check stores a denial entry for shortCacheTTL (30s). That entry is read at the top of Check, before the cached permissions and before the DB fallback. If a check runs in the window before a newly created dashboard/folder's permission rows are visible, the denial is cached. The same happens when an admin grants access to a resource the user was just denied. In both cases every later Check for that resource returns denied for up to 30s without consulting the DB. The DB requery, which this PR adds specifically to fix creator access, is skipped. Nothing invalidates denial entries when permissions change.

findings.title: DB fallback still uses the cached folder tree, so access via a newly created parent folder is denied and the denial cached
findings.body: On a cache miss or stale-cache deny, Check re-fetches permissions from the DB. checkPermission then calls checkInheritedPermissions, which uses buildFolderTree, served from folderCache (30s TTL). A folder created after the tree was cached has no ancestors in that tree. If the user's grant is on an ancestor of the new folder, the check fails even with fresh permissions, and the result is written to the denial cache. Newly created folder hierarchies therefore still yield false denials for up to 30s, which is the scenario this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because '_' can appear inside names and folder UIDs
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with '_', and resource names and folder UIDs may contain underscores. For example, (name="a_b", parent="") and (name="a", parent="b_") both produce "..._a_b_". A denial recorded for one resource/folder pair is then returned for a different one, giving a false deny for up to 30s. Use a separator that cannot occur in these values, or encode the components.

findings.title: Every deny on cached permissions now triggers a full DB permission query
findings.body: Previously a warm permCache answered Check entirely from cache. Now any check that is denied from cached permissions falls through to getIdentityPermissions. That path issues team, basic-role and permission queries; getUserPermissions no longer consults the cache. Singleflight only collapses concurrent identical requests, and the denial cache is per resource. A user checked against many resources they cannot access, such as filtering a dashboard list with per-item Check, now causes one DB round trip per denied resource every 30s. This can substantially increase DB load.

findings.title: List still serves stale cached permissions, so newly created resources are missing from listings
findings.body: List returns the cached permission map whenever one exists and never requeries. A dashboard or folder the user just created (and only has a direct grant on) will not appear in List results for up to 30s. This is inconsistent with Check, which now falls back to the DB, and leaves part of the described problem unfixed.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not prove the denial cache short-circuits
findings.body: The comment says the permCache entry grants access, but it sets {"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats that as not allowed. The DB fallback also returns no permissions, because the default fakeStore has none. The test would therefore pass with the denial cache removed entirely. The cache entry should be true, and the store should grant access, so the test actually verifies the short-circuit.
